description.value: The study evaluated three cognitive reappraisal strategies and craving suppression during viewing of palatable food images in adolescents using fMRI.

spans.text: Herein we evaluated the efficacy of a broader range of reappraisal strategies in modulating neural responsivity to palatable food images among individuals who ranged from lean to obese

value: Participants showed greater activation in the left medial superior frontal gyrus, left ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, and right posterior cerebellar lobe, and less activation in the left supramarginal gyrus in response to the costs of eating versus imagine eating contrast.

The costs of eating reappraisal strategy versus imagined intake of food resulted in greater activation in the medial superior frontal gyrus, ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, and posterior cerebellar lobe and less activation in the supramarginal gyrus. These findings suggest that the strategy modulates inhibitory and attention-related region activation in response to palatable food images.

instructions.value: On each trial, participants were instructed to think about the food image in one of four ways: imagine eating, think about the long-term costs of eating the food, think about the long-term benefits of not eating the food, or suppress craving. They received a 2-second instruction cue before a 5-second stimulus presentation and practiced the strategies for 10 minutes before scanning.

stimuli.value: Food photographs selected from 128 images based on individual preferences: 20 most appetizing and 20 least appetizing images. Images represented fruits, discretionary foods, grains, dairy, fats and oils, vegetables, mixed dishes, and protein foods.

spans.text: Food images ( 30 ) included fruits (e.g., blueberries, cherries), discretionary foods (e.g., brownies, French fries), grains (breads, pastas), dairy (e.g., different types of cheeses), fats and oils (i.e., butter), vegetables (e.g., broccoli, peas), mixed dishes (e.g., a plate with eggs and hash browns), and protein (e.g., steak, seafood) ( 31 ).
